commits: 704536ab0 Wire the batched Q4 planar numerics into assembly and recovery (L4)
84810a7dc Publish batch rows in assembly order and match the per-element backward error
scope: L4: formation cache misses of exact qualified Q4 planar elements run through one batched, bit-identical kernel (src/anyfesolver/_q4_planar_batch.py) inside the existing assembly lease
L4: default four-Gauss-point recovery of the same elements runs through the batched kernel inside the existing recovery lease
every per-element instance, quadrature, cache-key, admission and binding check stays per element
a runtime known-answer self-check of the emulated summation order gates the batch; any refusal, self-check failure or input failure reruns the whole batch through the per-element path
minimum batch sizes: 96 formation rows, 128 recovery rows; below them the per-element loops run unchanged
batch-formed rows are bound only when the ordered per-element assembly loop reaches them

contract_notes: D2: a foreign mutate-and-restore of the mesh during the single revision_signature observation is outside the contract; persistent mutations are still refused at the lease boundaries
a runtime-authority generation move during the shared batch kernel, which belongs to no single element, discards the batch and reruns every element per element under the new generation
in error cases, cache-hit elements that precede a failing element may already be bound when the error is raised
both differences are visible only outside a lease; the caller sees the same error and state

decisions.D1: keep the runtime-authority generation bracket of each replaced guarded call, through a private hook, with regression tests
decisions.D2: accept: the batched formation observes the mesh revision_signature once per element (the caller's cache key) and checks that the coordinates it reads reproduce the key's relative-coordinate entry, instead of recomputing the key inside the formation

owner_decisions.trust_boundary: NumPy/Numba/SciPy/Python builtins, the compensated contraction modules and ANYfeSolver classes and guard machinery are not rebound at run time; hostile data, instance attributes and subclasses stay in scope and are refused or sent to the per-element path; mid-request mutation is out of contract
